title: Child reunification packet
summary: Prepare verified identity, authorised contacts, meeting points, medical needs, and release rules before separation occurs.
content: Practical sequence: Use current photos, names, trusted contacts, school or care details, allergies, communication needs, two meeting points, and a rule never to release the child to an unverified person. Define the exact decision, responsible person, deadline, and next review for “Child reunification packet”. Separate verified facts from assumptions, requests, and unconfirmed reports for “Child reunification packet”. Record resources issued, people affected, consent limits, and unresolved risks for “Child reunification packet”. Use a second checker for important totals, names, routes, or safety decisions for “Child reunification packet”. Close the cycle with a dated handover and one clearly assigned next action for “Child reunification packet”. Do not expose private identity, health, location, or contact details beyond genuine need in “Child reunification packet”. Urgency does not justify coercion, discrimination, theft, humiliation, or secret decisions in “Child reunification packet”.

title: Older-adult medicine and support copy
summary: Keep a portable, dated copy of essential medicines, allergies, conditions, devices, routines, contacts, and decision-support needs.
content: Working sequence: Store one copy with the person, one with the emergency kit, and one trusted off-site copy, updating all after every professional change.
